title.zh: 卷一百三十五 列傳第二十三 陳遇 葉兌 范常 宋思顏 郭景祥 楊元杲 阮弘道 孔克仁
title.en: Volume 135 Biographies 23: Chen Yu, Ye Dui, Fan Chang, Song Siyan, Guo Jingxiang, Yang Yuangao, Ruan Hongdao, Kong Keren
title.raw: 卷一百三十五 列傳第二十三 陳遇 葉兌 范常 宋思顏 郭景祥 楊元杲 阮弘道 孔克仁 Volume 135 Biographies 23: Chen Yu, Ye Dui, Fan Chang, Song Siyan, Guo Jingxiang, Yang Yuangao, Ruan Hongdao, Kong Keren

sentences.zh: 陳遇，字中行，先世曹人。

translations.literal: Chen Yu, style name Zhongxing, his forebears were men of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu, courtesy name Zhongxing, came from a family originally of Cao.

sentences.zh: 高祖義甫，宋翰林學士，徙居建康，子孫因家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yifu was a Song Hanlin Academician; he moved to reside at Jiankang, and descendants thereby made it their home.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yifu had been a Hanlin Academician under the Song; he relocated to Jiankang, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 遇天資沉粹，篤學博覽，精象數之學。

translations.literal: Chen by nature was deep and pure, devoted in study and broad in reading, and refined in the learning of signs and numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was by nature grave and refined, a devoted scholar of wide learning who excelled in astronomy, calendrics, and divination.

sentences.zh: 元末為溫州教授，已而棄官歸隱。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he was professor at Wenzhou; before long he abandoned office and returned to seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuan dynasty he served as an instructor in Wenzhou, but soon resigned and withdrew into private life.

sentences.zh: 學者稱為靜誠先生。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master Jingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars addressed him as Master Jingcheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖渡江，以秦從龍薦，發書聘之，引伊、呂、諸葛為喻。

translations.literal: When the Founder crossed the river, on Qin Conglong's recommendation he sent a letter to engage him, citing Yi, Lü, and Zhuge as analogies.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founder crossed the Yangzi, Qin Conglong recommended him; the Founder sent a letter of invitation comparing Chen to Yi Yin, Lü Shang, and Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 遇至，與語，大悅，遂留參密議，日見親信。

translations.literal: When Chen arrived and he conversed with him, he was greatly pleased; thereupon he was kept to take part in secret deliberations, day by day growing trusted.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen arrived and they spoke together, the Founder was delighted and kept him for confidential counsel, growing more trusting of him each day.

sentences.zh: 太祖為吳王，授供奉司丞，辭。

translations.literal: When the Founder was King of Wu, he was appointed Attendant of the Service Bureau; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder was still King of Wu, Chen was offered the post of deputy director of the Service Bureau, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 即皇帝位，三授翰林學士，皆辭。

translations.literal: Upon assuming the imperial throne, three times he was granted Hanlin Academician; each time he declined.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, Chen was three times offered the rank of Hanlin Academician, and each time he refused.

sentences.zh: 乃賜肩輿一乘，衛士十人護出入，以示榮寵。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted one sedan chair and ten guards to escort him in going out and coming in, to show honor and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Instead the Emperor gave him a sedan chair and ten guards to attend him whenever he went abroad, as a mark of special honor.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，奉命至浙江廉察民隱，還賜金帛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, on orders he went to Zhejiang to investigate and examine the people's hidden grievances; on his return he was bestowed gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 he was sent to Zhejiang to inquire into the people's grievances; when he returned, the court rewarded him with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 除中書左丞，又辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Vice President of the Secretariat; again he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left vice president of the Secretariat, but again declined.

sentences.zh: 明年召對華蓋殿，賜坐，命草《平西詔》。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned for audience in Huagai Hall, granted a seat, and ordered to draft the "Edict on Pacifying the West."
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned to audience in Huagai Hall, given a seat, and ordered to draft the Edict on Pacifying the West.

sentences.zh: 授禮部侍郎，兼弘文館大學士，復辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall; again he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of rites and concurrent grand academician of the Hongwen Hall, but once more refused.

sentences.zh: 西域進良馬，遇引漢故事以諫。

translations.literal: The Western Regions presented fine horses; Chen cited Han precedents to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Regions sent fine horses as tribute, Chen cited Han-dynasty precedents in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 除太常少卿，固辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 強之，不可。

translations.literal: They pressed him; he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the appointment on him, but he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 最後除禮部尚書，又固辭。

translations.literal: Finally he was appointed Minister of Rites; again he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: At last he was made minister of rites, and again firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝沉吟良久，從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor pondered for a long while and assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hesitated a long while, then yielded to his wish.

sentences.zh: 自是不復強以官。

translations.literal: From then on he was no longer pressed with office.
translations.idiomatic: After that the court no longer tried to force an office on him.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容言欲官其子，遇曰：「臣三子皆幼，學未成，請俟異日。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once spoke at ease, saying he wished to give office to Chen's sons. Chen said: "Your servant's three sons are all young; their studies are not complete—please wait for another day."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once remarked in an easy tone that he wished to appoint Chen's sons. Chen replied, "Your servant's three sons are still young and have not finished their studies; I beg that Your Majesty wait for another day."

sentences.zh: 帝亦弗強也。

translations.literal: The Emperor likewise did not press.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not press the matter either.

sentences.zh: 遇自開基之始，即侍帷幄。

translations.literal: From the beginning of the founding of the state, Chen attended at the imperial curtains.
translations.idiomatic: From the very founding of the dynasty Chen had served at the imperial side.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問保國安民至計，遇對：「以不嗜殺人，薄斂，任賢，復先王禮樂為首務。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked the supreme plan for securing the state and settling the people. Chen answered: "Take as foremost tasks not being fond of killing people, light taxation, employing the worthy, and restoring the ritual and music of former kings."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor once asked him for the supreme policy to secure the realm and settle the people, Chen answered, "The foremost tasks are to refrain from bloodshed, keep taxes light, employ the worthy, and restore the ritual and music of the ancient kings."

sentences.zh: 廷臣或有過被譴責，遇力為解，多得全釋。

translations.literal: When court ministers at times had faults and were reprimanded and punished, Chen strove to intercede for them, and many were fully released.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials were faulted and punished, Chen often pleaded on their behalf, and many were spared.

sentences.zh: 其計畫多秘不傳，而寵禮之隆，勛戚大臣無與比者。

translations.literal: His plans were mostly secret and not transmitted, yet the loftiness of favor and ceremony shown him—no meritorious kinsmen or great ministers could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his counsel was kept secret, yet the honor the court showed him surpassed even that given to meritorious kinsmen and great ministers.

sentences.zh: 數監幸其第，語必稱「先生」，或呼為「君子」。

translations.literal: Several times the Emperor in person visited his residence; in speech he invariably called him "Master," or addressed him as "the gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor repeatedly visited his home in person, always addressing him as "Master" or calling him "the gentleman."

sentences.zh: 命爵輒辭，終成其高。

translations.literal: Whenever ennoblement was commanded he declined; in the end his loftiness was fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ennoblement was offered he declined, and in the end his reputation for lofty integrity was complete.

sentences.zh: 十七年卒，賜葬鐘山。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died; burial on Bell Mountain was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 17 of the reign and was granted burial on Bell Mountain.

sentences.zh: 子恭，舉人，累官工部尚書，有能聲。

translations.literal: His son Gong was a provincial graduate; through successive offices he rose to Minister of Works, with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gong, a provincial graduate, rose through the ranks to minister of works and won a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 遇弟遠，字中復，嘗隨遇侍帝。

translations.literal: Chen's younger brother Yuan, style name Zhongfu, once followed Chen in attending the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's younger brother Yuan, courtesy name Zhongfu, had once accompanied Chen in attendance on the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，為翰林待詔，精繪事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was a Hanlin awaiting edict, refined in painting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign he served as a Hanlin awaiting edict and excelled at painting.

sentences.zh: 遠子孟顒，善書。

translations.literal: Yuan's son Meng'ang was skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's son Meng'ang was accomplished in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 附 秦從龍

translations.literal: Appended: Qin Conglong
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Qin Conglong

sentences.zh: 秦從龍，字元之，洛陽人。

translations.literal: Qin Conglong, style name Yuanzhi, was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Conglong, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was a native of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 仕元，官江南行台侍御史。

translations.literal: He served the Yuan; his office was Attending Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan he served as an attending censor on the Jiangnan regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 兵亂，避居鎮江。

translations.literal: When soldiers rioted, he avoided trouble and dwelt at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the military turmoil he took refuge in Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 徐達之攻鎮江也，太祖謂之曰：「聞有秦元之者，才器老成，汝當詢訪，致吾欲見意。」

translations.literal: When Xu Da attacked Zhenjiang, the Founder said to him: "I have heard there is one Qin Yuanzhi, whose talent and capacity are seasoned and mature—you should inquire and seek him out, and convey my wish to see him."
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da was attacking Zhenjiang, the Founder told him, "I have heard of a Qin Yuanzhi, a man of seasoned talent—you should seek him out and convey my wish to meet him."

sentences.zh: 達下鎮江，訪得之。

translations.literal: Xu Da took Zhenjiang, sought him out, and obtained him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da took the city, found him, and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 太祖命從子文正、甥李文忠奉金綺造其廬聘焉。

translations.literal: The Founder ordered his nephew Wen Zheng and his sister's son Li Wenzhong to bear gold and brocade and go to his dwelling to engage him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent his nephew Guo Wen Zheng and his nephew Li Wenzhong with gifts of gold and brocade to Qin's home to invite him.

sentences.zh: 從龍與妻陳偕來，太祖自迎之於龍江。

translations.literal: Conglong came together with his wife Chen; the Founder himself went out to welcome them at Longjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Conglong came with his wife Chen, and the Founder went in person to welcome them at Longjiang.

sentences.zh: 時太祖居富民家，因邀從龍與同處，朝夕訪以時事。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder lodged at a rich man's house; he therefore invited Conglong to dwell together and morning and evening sought his counsel on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Founder was staying at a wealthy household; he invited Conglong to lodge with him and consulted him morning and evening on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 已，即元御史台為府，居從龍西華門外，事無大小悉與之謀。

translations.literal: Before long, taking the Yuan Censorate as the headquarters, he lodged Conglong outside the Xihua Gate; matters great and small were all deliberated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, having made the former Yuan censorate his headquarters, he housed Conglong just outside the Xihua Gate and consulted him on every matter, large or small.

sentences.zh: 嘗以筆書漆簡，問答甚密，左右皆不能知。

translations.literal: At times he wrote with the brush on lacquered slips; question and answer were very close, and those at his side could not know.
translations.idiomatic: They sometimes exchanged written questions and answers on lacquered slips so privately that even those close at hand could not tell what was discussed.

sentences.zh: 從龍生日，太祖與世子厚有贈遺，或親至其家燕飲。

translations.literal: On Conglong's birthday the Founder and the heir apparent made generous gifts, or the Founder in person came to his house for a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: On Conglong's birthday the Founder and the heir apparent sent lavish gifts, and sometimes the Founder came in person to feast at his home.

sentences.zh: 至正二十五年冬，從龍子澤死，請告歸。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-fifth year of Zhizheng, Conglong's son Ze died; he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Zhizheng year 25, Conglong's son Ze died, and he asked leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 太祖出郊握手送之。

translations.literal: The Founder went out beyond the suburbs, clasped his hand, and saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder went out beyond the suburbs, took his hand, and saw him off.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒，年七十，太祖驚悼。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness, aged seventy; the Founder was startled and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died of illness at the age of seventy, and the Founder was shocked and deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 時方督軍至鎮江，親臨哭之，厚恤其家，命有司營葬。

translations.literal: At that time he was just directing the army to Zhenjiang; he came in person to weep for him, richly comforted his family, and ordered the officials to arrange the burial.
translations.idiomatic: He was then directing troops toward Zhenjiang, but came in person to mourn him, gave his family generous relief, and ordered the authorities to arrange the funeral.

sentences.zh: 葉兌，字良仲，寧海人。

translations.literal: Ye Dui, style name Liangzhong, was a man of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Dui, courtesy name Liangzhong, was a native of Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 以經濟自負，尤精天文、地理、卜筮之書。

translations.literal: He prided himself on statecraft and economics, and was especially refined in books on astronomy, geography, and divination.
translations.idiomatic: He prided himself on statecraft and was especially expert in astronomy, geography, and divination.

sentences.zh: 元末，知天運有歸，以布衣獻書太祖。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, knowing that Heaven's mandate had a destination, as a commoner he presented a memorial to the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuan, seeing that the mandate of Heaven was shifting, he submitted a written plan to the Founder as a private citizen.

sentences.zh: 列一綱三目，言天下大計。

translations.literal: He set forth one main theme and three sub-points, speaking of the great plan for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: It laid out one overarching strategy and three subsidiary points on the grand design for the empire.

sentences.zh: 時太祖已定寧越，規取張士誠、方國珍。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder had already secured Ning and Yue and was planning to take Zhang Shicheng and Fang Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Founder had already secured Ningbo and Shaoxing and was planning to seize the domains of Zhang Shicheng and Fang Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 而察罕兵勢甚盛，遣使至金陵招太祖，故兌書於三者籌之為詳。

translations.literal: Yet Chaghan's military power was very strong, and he sent envoys to Jinling to recruit the Founder; therefore in his memorial Ye deliberated on the three in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Chaghan Temür's armies were very strong and had sent envoys to Jinling to win the Founder over, so Ye's memorial weighed all three rivals in careful detail.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: Its summary said:
translations.idiomatic: The gist of it read:

sentences.zh: 愚聞：取天下者，必有一定之規模。

translations.literal: This foolish one has heard: he who takes the realm must have a fixed plan and pattern.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that whoever would take the realm must follow a fixed strategic design.

sentences.zh: 韓信初見高祖，畫楚、漢成敗；

translations.literal: When Han Xin first met the High Ancestor, he mapped the rise and fall of Chu and Han;
translations.idiomatic: When Han Xin first met Emperor Gaozu of Han, he mapped out the contest between Chu and Han;

sentences.zh: 孔明臥草廬，與先主論三分形勢者是也。

translations.literal: Kongming lying in a thatched hut and discussing with the Former Lord the tripartite situation—such was the case.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhuge Liang, still in his thatched hut, discussed the three-way balance of power with the Former Lord—such were the models.

sentences.zh: 今之規模，宜北絕李察罕，南並張九四。

translations.literal: Today's plan and pattern should cut off Li Chaghan to the north and merge Zhang Jiusi to the south.
translations.idiomatic: The design for today should be to break off relations with Chaghan Temür in the north and absorb Zhang Shicheng in the south.

sentences.zh: 撫溫、台，取閩、越，定都建康，拓地江、廣。

translations.literal: Pacify Wen and Tai, take Min and Yue, fix the capital at Jiankang, and extend territory through Jiang and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Pacify Wenzhou and Taizhou, seize Fujian and Zhejiang, make Jiankang the capital, and extend your territory along the Yangzi and the coast.

sentences.zh: 進則越兩淮以北征，退則畫長江而自守。

translations.literal: Advancing, cross the two Huai and campaign north; retreating, take the long Yangzi as boundary and hold it yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you advance, cross the Huai and campaign north; if you hold back, take the long Yangzi as your line of defense.

sentences.zh: 夫金陵，古稱龍蟠虎踞帝王之都。

translations.literal: As for Jinling, in antiquity it was called a capital where the dragon coils and the tiger crouches.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling has since antiquity been called a capital where dragon and tiger coil—a seat fit for an emperor.

sentences.zh: 藉其兵力資財，以攻則克，以守則固，百察罕能如吾何哉？

translations.literal: Relying on its military strength and resources, in attack you conquer, in defense you are firm—how can Chaghan in a hundred ways do anything to us?
translations.idiomatic: With its armies and wealth behind you, you will conquer when you attack and stand firm when you defend—what can Chaghan do against you?

sentences.zh: 江之所備，莫急上流。

translations.literal: Of what the Yangzi requires for defense, nothing is more urgent than the upper reaches.
translations.idiomatic: In defending the Yangzi, nothing is more urgent than securing the upper river.

sentences.zh: 今義師已克江州，足蔽全吳。

translations.literal: Now the righteous army has already taken Jiangzhou, sufficient to screen all Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Your army has already taken Jiangzhou, which is enough to shield all of Wu.

sentences.zh: 況自滁、和至廣陵，皆吾所有。

translations.literal: Moreover from Chu, He, to Guangling—all are ours.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from Chuzhou and Hezhou down to Guangling, all is already yours.

sentences.zh: 非直守江，兼可守淮矣。

translations.literal: It is not only defending the Yangzi—you can also defend the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: You can defend not only the Yangzi but the Huai as well.

sentences.zh: 張氏傾覆可坐而待，淮東諸郡亦將來歸。

translations.literal: Zhang's collapse can be awaited seated; the various commanderies east of the Huai will also come to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's fall can be awaited at leisure, and the commanderies east of the Huai will soon submit as well.

sentences.zh: 北略中原，李氏可並也。

translations.literal: Campaigning north into the Central Plain, Li's [domain] can also be merged.
translations.idiomatic: When you campaign north into the Central Plain, Li's territory can be absorbed as well.

sentences.zh: 今聞察罕妄自尊大，致書明公，如曹操之招孫權。

translations.literal: Now I hear Chaghan presumptuously holds himself high and sends a letter to Your Excellency, like Cao Cao recruiting Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Chaghan has grown arrogant and sent Your Excellency a letter like Cao Cao's invitation to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 竊以元運將終，人心不屬，而察罕欲效操所為，事勢不侔。

translations.literal: I venture to think the Yuan mandate is nearing its end and men's hearts do not belong to it, yet Chaghan wishes to imitate what Cao did—the circumstances do not match.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the Yuan mandate is near its end and the people's hearts are no longer with it, yet Chaghan wishes to play Cao Cao's part—the situation does not match.

sentences.zh: 宜如魯肅計，鼎足江東，以觀天下之釁，此其大綱也。

translations.literal: You should follow Lu Su's plan, stand on three feet in Jiangdong, and watch for openings in the realm—this is the main outline.
translations.idiomatic: You should follow Lu Su's plan, hold a tripartite footing east of the Yangzi, and watch for openings in the realm—that is the overarching strategy.

sentences.zh: 至其目有三。

translations.literal: As for its sub-points, there are three.
translations.idiomatic: The three subsidiary points are as follows.

sentences.zh: 張九四之地，南包杭、紹，北跨通、泰，而以平江為巢穴。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiusi's territory south embraces Hang and Shao, north spans Tong and Tai, and takes Pingjiang as its nest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng's territory runs south through Hangzhou and Shaoxing, north across Nantong and Taizhou, with Pingjiang as his stronghold.

sentences.zh: 今欲攻之，莫若聲言掩取杭、紹、湖、秀，而大兵直搗平江。

translations.literal: If you now wish to attack him, nothing is better than proclaiming you will seize Hang, Shao, Hu, and Xiu, while the main army strikes straight at Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: To attack him now, it would be best to announce a feint against Hangzhou, Shaoxing, Huzhou, and Jiaxing while the main force strikes directly at Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 城固難以驟拔，則以鎖城法困之。

translations.literal: If the city is strong and hard to seize in a rush, then use the method of locking the city to wear him down.
translations.idiomatic: If the city is too strong to take quickly, use the encirclement method to wear him down.

sentences.zh: 於城外矢石不到之地別築長圍，分命將卒四面立營，屯田固守，斷其出入之路。

translations.literal: Outside the city, in a place where arrows and stones cannot reach, separately build a long encirclement; divide orders to generals and soldiers to set camps on four sides, garrison fields and hold firm, and cut off his roads of going out and coming in.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond range of missiles, build an outer cordon; station troops in camps on all four sides, farm the fields, hold the line, and cut off every route in or out.

sentences.zh: 分兵略定屬邑，收其稅糧以贍軍中。

translations.literal: Divide troops to pacify subordinate districts, collect their tax grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Send detachments to secure the surrounding districts and levy their grain to feed your army.

sentences.zh: 彼坐守空城，安得不困？

translations.literal: He sits guarding an empty city—how can he not be worn down?
translations.idiomatic: Trapped in an empty city, how can he fail to be worn down?

sentences.zh: 平江既下，巢穴已傾，杭、越必歸，余郡解體。

translations.literal: Once Pingjiang is taken, the nest is already overturned; Hang and Yue will surely submit, and the remaining commanderies will dissolve.
translations.idiomatic: Once Pingjiang falls, his stronghold is gone; Hangzhou and Shaoxing will submit, and the other districts will collapse.

sentences.zh: 此上計也。

translations.literal: This is the upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: This is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 張氏重鎮在紹興。

translations.literal: Zhang's key stronghold is at Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's chief stronghold lies at Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 紹興懸隔江海，所以數攻而不克者，以彼糧道在三江斗門也。

translations.literal: Shaoxing hangs separated by river and sea; the reason for repeated attacks without success is that their grain route lies at the Sanjiang sluice gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing lies across river and sea; the reason repeated attacks have failed is that their supply line runs through the Sanjiang sluice.

sentences.zh: 若一軍攻平江，斷其糧道；

translations.literal: If one army attacks Pingjiang and cuts off their grain route;
translations.idiomatic: If one army attacks Pingjiang and cuts their supply line,

sentences.zh: 一軍攻杭州，絕其援兵，紹興必拔。

translations.literal: one army attacks Hangzhou and severs their relief troops—Shaoxing will surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: and another attacks Hangzhou and blocks their reinforcements, Shaoxing will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 所攻在蘇、杭，所取在紹興，所謂多方以誤之者也。

translations.literal: What is attacked is Su and Hang; what is taken is Shaoxing—this is what is called using many directions to confuse the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: You strike at Suzhou and Hangzhou but take Shaoxing—this is the tactic of confusing the enemy on many fronts.

sentences.zh: 紹興既拔，杭城勢孤，湖、秀風靡，然後進攻平江，犁其心腹，江北餘孽隨而瓦解。

translations.literal: Once Shaoxing is taken, Hangzhou city's position is isolated; Hu and Xiu bow to the wind; then advance to attack Pingjiang, plow its heart and belly, and the remaining spawn north of the river follow in dissolution.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shaoxing is taken, Hangzhou stands alone, Huzhou and Jiaxing will follow, and then you can advance on Pingjiang and strike at his core; his remaining forces north of the river will collapse in turn.

sentences.zh: 此次計也。

translations.literal: This is the second plan.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second-best plan.

sentences.zh: 方國珍狼子野心，不可馴狎。

translations.literal: Fang Guozhen has the heart of a wolf cub and cannot be tamed and made tractable.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guozhen has the heart of a wolf cub and cannot be tamed.

sentences.zh: 往年大兵取婺州，彼即奉書納款。

translations.literal: In former years when the great army took Wuzhou, he at once presented a letter submitting allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When your army took Wuzhou in earlier years, he promptly sent a letter of submission.

sentences.zh: 後遣夏煜、陳顯道招諭，彼復狐疑不從。

translations.literal: Later Xia Yu and Chen Xiandao were sent to summon and instruct him; again he was suspicious and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xia Yu and Chen Xiandao were sent to win him over, he wavered again and refused.

sentences.zh: 顧遣使從海道報元，謂江東委之納款，誘令張昶齎詔而來。

translations.literal: Yet he sent envoys by the sea route to report to the Yuan, saying he had entrusted Jiangdong's submission, and lured Zhang Chang to come bearing an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he also sent envoys by sea to report to the Yuan that he had entrusted Jiangdong's surrender, and induced Zhang Chang to come bearing an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 且遣韓叔義為說客，欲說明公奉詔。

translations.literal: Moreover he sent Han Shuyi as a persuader, wishing to persuade Your Excellency to accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He even sent Han Shuyi as an envoy to urge Your Excellency to accept the Yuan edict.

sentences.zh: 彼既降我，而反欲招我降元。

translations.literal: He had already submitted to us, yet in turn wished to recruit us to submit to the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Having already submitted to you, he then tried to recruit you to submit to the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 其反覆狡獪如是，宜興師問罪。

translations.literal: His reversals and cunning trickery being thus, you should raise troops to inquire into his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: His duplicity is such that you ought to raise an army and call him to account.

sentences.zh: 然彼以水為命，一聞兵至，挈家航海，中原步騎無如之何。

translations.literal: Yet he takes water as his life; once he hears troops arrive, he takes his family and goes to sea by ship—the Central Plain's infantry and cavalry can do nothing to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lives by the sea; at the first rumor of troops he will put his family aboard ship, and your northern infantry and cavalry can do nothing against him.

sentences.zh: 夫上兵攻心，彼言杭、趙一平，即當納土，不過欲款我師耳。

translations.literal: The supreme army attacks the mind; he says once Hang and Zhao are pacified he will at once yield territory—it is only that he wishes to stall our army.
translations.idiomatic: The highest form of warfare strikes at the mind: his promise to surrender once Hangzhou and Zhao are pacified is only a ruse to stall your army.

sentences.zh: 攻之之術，宜限以日期，責其歸順。

translations.literal: The method of attacking him should set a limit by date and charge him to return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: The way to attack him is to set a deadline and demand his submission.

sentences.zh: 彼自方國璋之沒，自知兵不可用。

translations.literal: Since Fang Guozhang's death, he himself knows his troops cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: Since the death of Fang Guozhang, he knows himself that his forces are useless.

sentences.zh: 又叔義還稱義師之盛，氣已先挫。

translations.literal: Moreover when Shuyi returned he praised the righteous army's strength; their spirit was already first broken.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Han Shuyi returned he spoke of how strong your army was, and their morale was already shaken.

sentences.zh: 今因陳顯道以自通，正可脅之而從也。

translations.literal: Now because Chen Xiandao has opened communication on his own behalf, you can justly coerce him into following.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has opened contact through Chen Xiandao, you can press him into submission.

sentences.zh: 事宜速不宜緩。

translations.literal: The affair should be swift and not slow.
translations.idiomatic: The matter calls for speed, not delay.

sentences.zh: 宣諭之後，更置官吏，拘集舟艦，潛收其兵權，以消未然之變。

translations.literal: After proclaiming and instructing him, replace the officials, gather ships, secretly take his military authority, to dispel changes not yet arisen.
translations.idiomatic: After you announce your demands, replace his officials, assemble his ships, and quietly strip him of military power to forestall any future revolt.

sentences.zh: 三郡可不勞而定。

translations.literal: The three commanderies can be settled without labor.
translations.idiomatic: The three coastal commanderies can be secured without a fight.

sentences.zh: 福建本浙江一道，兵脃城陋。

translations.literal: Fujian was originally one circuit of Zhejiang; its troops are weak and its cities crude.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian was originally part of the Zhejiang circuit; its armies are weak and its cities poor.

sentences.zh: 兩浙既平，必圖歸附。

translations.literal: Once the two Zhejiangs are pacified, it will surely plan to return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Once the two Zhejiangs are pacified, it will surely seek to submit.

sentences.zh: 下之一辯士力耳。

translations.literal: To take it requires only the effort of one debater.
translations.idiomatic: It would take no more than a single persuasive envoy.

sentences.zh: 如復稽遲，則大兵自溫、處入，奇兵自海道入，福州必不支。

translations.literal: If you again delay, then the great army will enter from Wen and Chu, and surprise troops will enter by the sea route—Fuzhou will surely not hold.
translations.idiomatic: If you delay again, your main force can enter from Wenzhou and Chuzhou while a flanking force comes by sea, and Fuzhou will not hold.

sentences.zh: 福州下，旁郡迎刃解矣。

translations.literal: Once Fuzhou falls, neighboring commanderies will split like bamboo against the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fuzhou falls, the neighboring districts will collapse like bamboo split by a knife.

sentences.zh: 威聲已震，然後進取兩廣，猶反掌也。

translations.literal: Once prestige and fame already shake the realm, then advance to take the two Guangs—it is still like turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Once your prestige has shaken the south, taking the two Guang provinces will be as easy as turning your hand.

sentences.zh: 太祖奇其言，欲留用之，力辭去。

translations.literal: The Founder marveled at his words and wished to keep and employ him; he firmly declined and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was impressed by his counsel and wished to keep him in service, but Ye firmly declined and departed.

sentences.zh: 賜銀幣襲衣。

translations.literal: He was granted silver, silks, and a robe of investiture.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded him with silver, silk, and a ceremonial robe.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，削平天下，規模次第，略如兌言。

translations.literal: Several years later, having cut down and pacified the realm, the plan and pattern in sequence were largely as Ye had said.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the Founder had pacified the realm, and the course of conquest followed Ye's design in broad outline.

sentences.zh: 范常，字子權，滁人。

translations.literal: Fan Chang, style name Ziquan, was a man of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chang, courtesy name Ziquan, was a native of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖軍滁，杖策謁軍門。

translations.literal: When the Founder's army was at Chu, leaning on his staff he visited the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder's army was at Chuzhou, he came to the camp leaning on his staff.

sentences.zh: 太祖夙知其名，與語意合，留置幕下。

translations.literal: The Founder had long known his name; in conversation their ideas accorded, and he was kept below the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder had long known his reputation; they spoke together and found their views in accord, and Fan was kept on the staff.

sentences.zh: 有疑輒問，常悉以實對。

translations.literal: When there were doubts he would at once ask; Fan always answered fully with truth.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Founder had doubts he would ask Fan, who always answered frankly.

sentences.zh: 諸將克和州，兵不戢。

translations.literal: The generals took Hezhou, but the troops would not restrain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals took Hezhou, the troops would not restrain themselves.

sentences.zh: 常言於太祖曰：「得一城而使人肝腦塗地，何以成大事？」

translations.literal: Fan said to the Founder: "Gaining one city yet making men's livers and brains smear the ground—how can you accomplish a great undertaking?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan said to the Founder, "If you win a city only to leave the people slaughtered, how can you accomplish anything great?"

sentences.zh: 太祖乃切責諸將。

translations.literal: The Founder thereupon sternly reproached the generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder then sternly rebuked the generals.

sentences.zh: 搜軍中所掠婦女，還其家，民大悅。

translations.literal: He searched out women seized in the army and returned them to their families; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He searched out the women seized by the troops and sent them home, and the people were greatly relieved.

sentences.zh: 太祖以四方割據，戰爭無虛日，命常為文，禱於上帝。

translations.literal: Because the four quarters were carved up and warfare had no idle day, the Founder ordered Fan to compose a text and pray to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm divided and war unceasing, the Founder ordered Fan to draft a prayer to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：「今天下紛紜，生民塗炭，不有所屬，物類盡矣。

translations.literal: Its words said: "Now the realm is in turmoil, the living people are charred on the coals; if they have no one to belong to, the kinds of things will be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: It read: "The realm is in turmoil and the people are in misery; unless they find a ruler to whom they can belong, all living things will perish.

sentences.zh: 倘元祚未終，則群雄當早伏其辜。

translations.literal: If the Yuan mandate is not yet ended, then the many heroes should early submit to their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: If the Yuan mandate is not yet exhausted, then let the rival warlords be punished first.

sentences.zh: 某亦在群雄中，請自某始。

translations.literal: I too am among the many heroes—please begin with me.
translations.idiomatic: I too am among those warlords; let the punishment begin with me.

sentences.zh: 若已厭元德，有天命者宜歸之，無使斯民久阽危苦。

translations.literal: If already weary of the Yuan's virtue, whoever has Heaven's mandate should be followed; do not let this people long stand in peril and suffering.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven has already turned from the Yuan, let those with the mandate be followed, and do not let the people suffer in danger any longer.

sentences.zh: 存亡之機，驗於三月。」

translations.literal: The hinge of survival and destruction will be tested in three months."
translations.idiomatic: Whether we survive or perish will be known within three months."

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其能達己意，命典文牘，授元帥府都事。

translations.literal: The Founder praised his ability to express the Founder's own intent and ordered him to oversee documents, appointing him Chief Clerk of the Marshal's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder praised him for voicing his own thoughts and put him in charge of documents, appointing him chief clerk of the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 取太平，命為知府，諭之曰：「太平，吾股肱郡，其民數困於兵，當令得所。」

translations.literal: When Taiping was taken, he was appointed prefect and instructed: "Taiping is my arm-and-thigh commandery; its people have repeatedly suffered from soldiers—you should let them find their place."
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping was taken, Fan was made prefect. The Founder told him, "Taiping is one of my core districts; its people have suffered repeatedly from war—you must give them relief."

sentences.zh: 常以簡易為治，興學恤民。

translations.literal: Fan always governed with simplicity and ease, raised schools, and comforted the people.
translations.idiomatic: Fan governed with simplicity, promoted schools, and cared for the people.

sentences.zh: 官廩有谷數千石，請給民乏種者，秋稔輸官，公私皆足。

translations.literal: The official granary had several thousand piculs of grain; he requested to give it to people lacking seed; in autumn when ripe they paid the government—public and private were both sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The government granary held several thousand piculs of grain; he lent seed to farmers in need, to be repaid after the autumn harvest, and both public and private stores were filled.

sentences.zh: 居三年，民親愛之，召入為侍儀。

translations.literal: After three years in office the people loved him dearly; he was summoned in as Attendant of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: After three years the people loved him, and he was recalled to serve as attendant of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，擢翰林直學士兼太常卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hanlin and concurrent Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 he was promoted to direct Hanlin academician and concurrent director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 帝銳意稽古禮文。

translations.literal: The Emperor was keen to examine antiquity's ritual texts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was intent on reviving ancient ritual and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 群臣集議，間有異同。

translations.literal: The ministers gathered to deliberate; at times there were differences.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers met to deliberate, their views sometimes differed.

sentences.zh: 常能參合眾言，委曲當上意。

translations.literal: Fan was able to combine the many opinions and tactfully match the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fan could reconcile the various opinions and shape them to satisfy the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋以病免歸。

translations.literal: Before long, on grounds of illness he was excused and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，手詔征詣闕，仍故官。

translations.literal: After more than a year, by handwritten edict he was summoned to the court and restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Emperor summoned him back by personal edict and restored his former post.

sentences.zh: 帝宴閒，輒命儒臣列坐，賦詩為樂。

translations.literal: At the Emperor's leisure banquets he would order Confucian ministers to sit in rows and compose poetry for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: At leisure banquets the Emperor would have the scholar-officials sit together and compose poetry for amusement.

sentences.zh: 常每先成，語多率。

translations.literal: Fan always finished first; his language was mostly unadorned.
translations.idiomatic: Fan always finished first, and his verse was plain and direct.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「老范詩質朴，殊似其為人也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said: "Old Fan's poetry is plain and unadorned—very much like the man himself."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and said, "Old Fan's poems are as plain as the man himself."

sentences.zh: 遷起居注。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Diarist of Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to diarist of attendance.

sentences.zh: 常有足疾，數在告，賜以安車。

translations.literal: Fan had a foot ailment and repeatedly took leave; he was granted a comfort carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Fan suffered from a foot ailment and often took leave; the Emperor granted him a comfort carriage.

sentences.zh: 尋乞歸，帝賦詩四章送之。

translations.literal: Before long he begged to return home; the Emperor composed four stanzas of poetry to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to retire, and the Emperor wrote four poems to see him off.

sentences.zh: 賜宅於太平。

translations.literal: A residence in Taiping was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a house in Taiping.

sentences.zh: 子祖，歷官雲南左參政，有修潔稱。

translations.literal: His son Zu through successive offices rose to Left Vice Commissioner of Yunnan, with a reputation for cultivated purity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zu rose to left vice commissioner of Yunnan and was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 附:潘庭堅

translations.literal: Appended: Pan Tingjian
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Pan Tingjian

sentences.zh: 潘庭堅，字叔聞，當塗人。

translations.literal: Pan Tingjian, style name Shuwen, was a man of Dangtu.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tingjian, courtesy name Shuwen, was a native of Dangtu.

sentences.zh: 元末為富陽教諭，謝去。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he was instructor at Fuyang and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuan he served as an instructor in Fuyang, then resigned.

sentences.zh: 太祖駐太平，以陶安薦，征庭堅為帥府教授。

translations.literal: When the Founder was stationed at Taiping, on Tao An's recommendation he summoned Tingjian as professor at the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder was at Taiping, Tao An recommended him, and Pan was summoned as professor at the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 慎密謙約，為太祖所稱。

translations.literal: Cautious, close, humble, and restrained—he was praised by the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Discreet, humble, and restrained, he won the Founder's praise.

sentences.zh: 下集慶，擢中書省博士。

translations.literal: When Jiqing was taken, he was promoted to Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the capture of Jiqing he was promoted to erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 婺州下，改為金華府，以庭堅同知府事。

translations.literal: When Wuzhou fell it was changed to Jinhua Prefecture; Tingjian was made to share prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzhou was taken and made Jinhua Prefecture, Pan was appointed to assist in governing it.

sentences.zh: 時上游諸郡次第平定，擇儒臣撫綏之。

translations.literal: At that time the various commanderies upriver were pacified in sequence; Confucian ministers were chosen to pacify and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: As the upstream districts were pacified one by one, the Founder chose scholar-officials to govern and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 先後用陶安、汪廣洋於江西，而庭堅與王愷守浙東。

translations.literal: In succession Tao An and Wang Guangyang were used in Jiangxi, while Tingjian and Wang Kai guarded eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Tao An and Wang Guangyang were sent in turn to Jiangxi, while Pan and Wang Kai held eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 太祖為吳王，設翰林院，與安同召為學士。

translations.literal: When the Founder was King of Wu he established the Hanlin Academy and summoned him together with An as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder became King of Wu he established the Hanlin Academy and summoned Pan and Tao An as academicians.

sentences.zh: 而庭堅已老，遂告歸。

translations.literal: But Tingjian was already old and thereupon requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Pan was already old by then and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年復召至，主會試。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu he was again summoned and presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 4 he was summoned again to preside over the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 子黼，字章甫。

translations.literal: His son Fu, style name Zhangfu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu, courtesy name Zhangfu.

sentences.zh: 有文名，官至江西按察使。

translations.literal: He had a literary reputation and through office rose to Regional Inspector of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He won a literary reputation and rose to regional inspector of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 會修律令，留為議律官。

translations.literal: When the statutes and ordinances were being revised, he was retained as an officer deliberating on law.
translations.idiomatic: When the legal code was being revised, he was retained as a legal deliberator.

sentences.zh: 書成，卒。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 黼謹飭類父，而文采清雅過之。

translations.literal: Fu was careful and disciplined like his father, yet his literary color was clear and elegant beyond him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was as disciplined as his father, but his literary style was more refined.

sentences.zh: 父子皆以鄉校顯，時以為榮。

translations.literal: Father and son both became illustrious through village schools; at the time this was considered glory.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both rose to prominence from local schooling, which was regarded at the time as a family honor.

sentences.zh: 宋思顏

translations.literal: Song Siyan
translations.idiomatic: Song Siyan

sentences.zh: 宋思顏，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Song Siyan—it is not known from what place he came.
translations.idiomatic: Song Siyan's place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 太祖克太平，以思顏居幕府。

translations.literal: When the Founder took Taiping, he had Siyan dwell in the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founder took Taiping, Song served in his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及定集慶，置江南行中書省，太祖總省事，以李善長及思顏為參議。

translations.literal: When Jiqing was secured, the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat was established; the Founder oversaw secretariat affairs, and Li Shanchang and Siyan were made Deliberators.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiqing was secured, the Jiangnan branch secretariat was established with the Founder as its chief; Li Shanchang and Song were made deliberators.

sentences.zh: 同時所設省中官李夢庚、郭景祥、侯元善、楊元杲、陶安、阮弘道、孔克仁、王愷、欒鳳、夏煜等數十人。

translations.literal: At the same time officials established in the secretariat included Li Menggeng, Guo Jingxiang, Hou Yuanshan, Yang Yuangao, Tao An, Ruan Hongdao, Kong Keren, Wang Kai, Luan Feng, Xia Yu, and several tens of others.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the secretariat included Li Menggeng, Guo Jingxiang, Hou Yuanshan, Yang Yuangao, Tao An, Ruan Hongdao, Kong Keren, Wang Kai, Luan Feng, Xia Yu, and dozens of others.

sentences.zh: 而思顏獨與善長並授參議，其任較諸人為重。

translations.literal: Yet Siyan alone with Shanchang was jointly granted Deliberator; his charge was heavier than the others'.
translations.idiomatic: Song alone shared the rank of deliberator with Li Shanchang, and his responsibilities were heavier than those of the others.

sentences.zh: 已，建大都督府，以思顏兼參軍事。

translations.literal: Before long the Great Military Commission was established, and Siyan was made concurrent Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when the great military commission was established, Song was also made a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗視事東閣，天暑，汗沾衣。

translations.literal: The Founder once conducted affairs in the Eastern Pavilion; the day was hot and sweat soaked his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while conducting business in the Eastern Pavilion on a hot day, sweat soaked the Founder's clothes.

sentences.zh: 左右更以衣進，皆數經浣濯者。

translations.literal: Those at his side changed and brought in clothes—all had been washed many times.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants brought fresh garments, all of them well-worn from repeated washing.

sentences.zh: 思顏曰：「主公躬行節儉，真可示法子孫，惟願終始如一。」

translations.literal: Siyan said: "My lord personally practices thrift and restraint—this truly can be shown as a model to sons and grandsons; I only wish it may be the same from beginning to end."
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "My lord practices thrift in person—a true model for your descendants; I only hope you will remain so to the end."

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其直，賜之幣。

translations.literal: The Founder praised his forthrightness and bestowed silks on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder praised his frankness and rewarded him with silk.

sentences.zh: 他日又進曰：「句容虎為害，既捕獲，宜除之，今豢養民間何益？」

translations.literal: Another day he again advanced and said: "The tiger at Jurong does harm; now that it has been captured, it should be eliminated—what use is it now to keep and raise it among the people?"
translations.idiomatic: On another day he said, "The tiger at Jurong has been doing harm; now that it has been captured, it ought to be killed—what good is it to keep it among the people?"

sentences.zh: 太祖欣然，即命殺虎。

translations.literal: The Founder was pleased and at once ordered the tiger killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder agreed at once and ordered the tiger killed.

sentences.zh: 其隨事納忠類如此。

translations.literal: His offering loyalty on each affair was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His loyal remonstrances on everyday matters were mostly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 後出為河南道按察僉事，坐事死。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Vice Commissioner of the Henan Circuit Surveillance Commission and died on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was sent out as vice commissioner of the Henan surveillance circuit and was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 附 夏煜

translations.literal: Appended: Xia Yu
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Xia Yu

sentences.zh: 夏煜，字允中，江寧人。

translations.literal: Xia Yu, style name Yunzhong, was a man of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yu, courtesy name Yunzhong, was a native of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 有俊才，工詩，辟為中書省博士。

translations.literal: He had outstanding talent, was skilled in poetry, and was recruited as Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He had outstanding talent and skill in poetry, and was recruited as a doctorate fellow of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 婺州平，調浙東分省，兩使方國珍，咸稱旨。

translations.literal: When Wuzhou was pacified, he was transferred to the eastern Zhe Branch Secretariat; twice sent as envoy to Fang Guozhen, and on both occasions won approval.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzhou was pacified, he was posted to the eastern Zhe branch secretariat; sent twice as envoy to Fang Guozhen, on both occasions to the Founder's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 太祖征陳友諒，儒臣惟劉基與煜侍。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Chen Youliang, among Confucian ministers only Liu Ji and Yu attended him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder campaigned against Chen Youliang, of the Confucian ministers only Liu Ji and Yu attended him.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽戰勝，太祖所與草檄賦詩者，煜其一也。

translations.literal: At the victory at Poyang, among those with whom the Founder drafted proclamations and composed poems, Yu was one.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Lake Poyang, among those with whom the Founder drafted proclamations and composed poems, Yu was one.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年使總制浙東諸府，與高見賢、楊憲、凌說四人以伺察搏擊為事，後俱以不良死。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year 1 he was sent to oversee the various prefectures of eastern Zhe; together with Gao Jianxian, Yang Xian, and Ling Shuo, the four of them made surveillance and persecution their business, and later all died for misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 he was sent to oversee the prefectures of eastern Zhe; together with Gao Jianxian, Yang Xian, and Ling Shuo, the four devoted themselves to surveillance and persecution, and later all died for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 郭景祥

translations.literal: Guo Jingxiang
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jingxiang

sentences.zh: 〈（李夢庚）〉

translations.literal: (Li Menggeng)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Li Menggeng)]〉

sentences.zh: 郭景祥，濠人。

translations.literal: Guo Jingxiang was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jingxiang was a native of Hao.

sentences.zh: 與鳳陽李夢庚皆從渡江，典文書，佐謀議，分任行中書省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: He and Li Menggeng of Fengyang both followed in crossing the river, managed documents, assisted in deliberation, and shared duties as Left and Right Bureau Directors of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Menggeng of Fengyang both crossed the Yangzi with the Founder, managed documents, assisted in planning, and served as left and right bureau directors of the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 既同調浙東分省，尋復同入為大都督府參軍。

translations.literal: Having been transferred together to the eastern Zhe Branch Secretariat, before long they again entered together as staff officers of the Great Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: They were later posted together to the eastern Zhe branch secretariat, then both returned as staff officers of the great military commission.

sentences.zh: 景祥性諒直，博涉書史，遇事敢言，太祖親信之。

translations.literal: Jingxiang's nature was sincere and upright; he broadly traversed books and histories; on affairs he dared speak— the Founder personally trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo was sincere and upright, widely read in history, and bold in speaking his mind; the Founder trusted him personally.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「景祥文吏，而有折衝禦侮才，能盡忠於我，可大任也。」

translations.literal: He once said: "Jingxiang is a civil clerk, yet has talent to repel foes and resist insult; he can exhaust loyalty to me—great charge can be given."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder once said, "Guo is a civil official, yet he has the talent to confront enemies and defend the realm; he can be utterly loyal to me and is fit for great responsibility."

sentences.zh: 先是，克滁州、太平、溧陽。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chuzhou, Taiping, and Liyang had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the army had taken Chuzhou, Taiping, and Liyang.

sentences.zh: 以城郭不完，輒命景祥董治之。

translations.literal: Because the city walls and moats were incomplete, he would at once order Jingxiang to supervise and repair them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the city defenses were incomplete, the Founder repeatedly put Guo in charge of repairing them.

sentences.zh: 既而和州守臣言，州城久廢，命景祥相度，即故址城之，九旬而工畢。

translations.literal: Before long the defending official of Hezhou reported that the prefectural city had long been abandoned; he ordered Jingxiang to survey and measure, and on the old site walled it—ninety days and the work was finished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hezhou garrison reported that the city walls had long lain in ruins, the Founder ordered Guo to survey the site and rebuild on the old foundations; the work was finished in ninety days.

sentences.zh: 太祖以為能，授和州總制。

translations.literal: The Founder considered him capable and appointed him Overall Controller of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder judged him capable and appointed him overall controller of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 景祥益治城隍樓櫓，廣屯田，練士卒，威望肅然。

translations.literal: Jingxiang further repaired city walls, moats, towers, and watchtowers, expanded garrison fields, drilled soldiers and officers, and his prestige and authority were solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Guo further strengthened the walls and towers, expanded garrison farming, drilled the troops, and his authority became formidable.

sentences.zh: 和遂為重鎮。

translations.literal: Hezhou thereupon became a key stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhou thus became a major stronghold.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒勞。

translations.literal: An imperial letter of commendation praised and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 仕終浙江行省參政。

translations.literal: In office he ended as Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served to the end as vice commissioner of the Zhejiang branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 謝再興之守諸全也，部將私販易吳境。

translations.literal: When Xie Zaixing was defending Zhuzhou, a subordinate general privately traded across the Wu border.
translations.idiomatic: While Xie Zaixing was defending Zhuzhou, one of his subordinates traded privately across the border into Wu territory.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒殺部將，召諭再興，命夢庚往諸全總制軍事。

translations.literal: The Founder in anger killed the subordinate general, summoned and instructed Zaixing, and ordered Menggeng to go to Zhuzhou as overall controller of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder had the subordinate executed in anger, summoned Xie to admonish him, and sent Li Menggeng to Zhuzhou to take overall command of the army.

sentences.zh: 再興還鎮，忿夢庚出己上，遂叛。

translations.literal: Zaixing returned to his command, resenting that Menggeng was placed above him, and thereupon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie returned to his post, resentful that Li had been placed over him, he rebelled.

sentences.zh: 執夢庚降於吳，夢庚死之。

translations.literal: They seized Menggeng and surrendered to Wu; Menggeng died for it.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Li Menggeng and surrendered him to Wu; Li was put to death.

sentences.zh: 其時，參佐行省者，又有毛騏、王濂。

translations.literal: At that time, among those assisting the branch secretariat, there were also Mao Qi and Wang Lian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, among those assisting the branch secretariat were also Mao Qi and Wang Lian.

sentences.zh: 附 王濂

translations.literal: Appended: Wang Lian
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Wang Lian

sentences.zh: 濂，字習古，定遠人，李善長婦兄也。

translations.literal: Lian, style name Xigu, was a man of Dingyuan; he was Li Shanchang's wife's older brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lian, courtesy name Xigu, was a native of Dingyuan and the elder brother of Li Shanchang's wife.

sentences.zh: 才嗜學，事親孝。

translations.literal: He was talented, devoted to learning, and filial in serving his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was gifted and devoted to study, and filial toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 初從汝、潁賊，太祖克集慶，乃渡江來歸。

translations.literal: At first he followed the Ru and Ying bandits; when the Founder took Jiqing, he crossed the river to submit.
translations.idiomatic: At first he followed the rebels of Ru and Ying; after the Founder took Jiqing, he crossed the Yangzi to submit.

sentences.zh: 善長為言，得召見，除執法官，讞獄平允。

translations.literal: Shanchang spoke on his behalf; he received a summons and audience, was appointed Judge of the Law, and his trial decisions were fair and even.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shanchang spoke on his behalf; he was summoned for an audience, appointed judge of the law, and his judgments were fair and even.

sentences.zh: 遷中書省員外郎，出為浙江按察僉事，治行著聞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat, then sent out as vice commissioner of the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission; his conduct in office was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, then sent out as vice commissioner of the Zhejiang surveillance commission, where his record in office won wide notice.

sentences.zh: 大風晝晦，濂應詔言民瘼，請緩征。

translations.literal: A great wind darkened the day at noon; Lian responded to the edict to speak on the people's sufferings and requested that levies be relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: When a great wind darkened the sky at midday, Wang responded to an imperial summons to speak on the people's hardships and asked that levies be eased.

sentences.zh: 太祖納之。

translations.literal: The Founder accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Hongwu year 3.

sentences.zh: 帝謂善長曰：「濂有王佐才，今死，朕失一臂。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Shanchang: "Lian had the talent of a royal minister; now that he is dead, I have lost an arm."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Li Shanchang, "Wang had the talent of a king's minister; now that he is dead, I have lost an arm."

sentences.zh: 後善長坐事，帝嘆曰：「使王濂在，必不至是。」

translations.literal: Later Shanchang was implicated in a case; the Emperor sighed and said: "If Wang Lian had been alive, it would surely not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Li Shanchang was implicated in a case, the Emperor sighed and said, "If Wang Lian had still been alive, things would surely not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 附 毛騏

translations.literal: Appended: Mao Qi
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Mao Qi

sentences.zh: 騏，字國祥，與濂同里。

translations.literal: Qi, style name Guoxiang, was from the same district as Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Qi, courtesy name Guoxiang, was from the same district as Wang Lian.

sentences.zh: 太祖自濠引兵趨定遠，騏扶縣令出降。

translations.literal: When the Founder led troops from Hao toward Dingyuan, Qi helped the magistrate out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder led troops from Hao toward Dingyuan, Mao helped the county magistrate come out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜，留與飲食，籌兵事，悉當意。

translations.literal: The Founder was pleased, kept him for food and drink, and discussed military affairs with him—all accorded with his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was pleased, kept him to dine with him, and discussed military affairs; everything Mao said accorded with his wishes.

sentences.zh: 取滁州，擢總管府經歷。

translations.literal: When Chuzhou was taken, he was promoted to manager of the General Administration.
translations.idiomatic: After Chuzhou was taken, he was promoted to manager of the general administration.

sentences.zh: 典倉廩，兼掌晨昏歷，稽將帥之失伍者。

translations.literal: He managed the granaries, also kept the calendar of dawn and dusk watches, and checked commanders absent from their posts.
translations.idiomatic: He managed the granaries, also kept the schedule of dawn and dusk watches, and inspected commanders who were absent from their posts.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，擢兵省郎中。

translations.literal: Following the crossing of the river, he was promoted to director of the Military Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangzi, he was promoted to director in the military secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時太祖左右惟善長及騏，文書機密，皆兩人協贊。

translations.literal: At that time at the Founder's side there were only Shanchang and Qi; confidential documents—all were jointly handled by the two of them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only Li Shanchang and Mao Qi stood at the Founder's side; confidential documents were all handled jointly by the two of them.

sentences.zh: 尋授參議官。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Deliberator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed deliberator.

sentences.zh: 征婺州，命權理中書省事，委以心膂。

translations.literal: When campaigning for Wuzhou, he was ordered to provisionally manage Secretariat affairs and was entrusted as the Founder's heart and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Wuzhou, he was ordered to manage Secretariat affairs on a provisional basis and was entrusted as the Founder's right-hand man.

sentences.zh: 俄病卒，太祖親為文哭之，臨視其葬。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness; the Founder personally composed a eulogy and wept for him, and attended his burial in person.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness; the Founder personally composed a funeral elegy and wept for him, and attended the burial in person.

sentences.zh: 子驤，管軍千戶，積功擢親軍指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His son Ziang was a commander of a thousand households; by accumulated merit he was promoted to assistant commander of the Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziang served as a commander of a thousand households and, by accumulated merit, was promoted to assistant commander of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 從定中原，進指揮使。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of the Central Plains, he advanced to commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of the Central Plains, he was promoted to commander.

sentences.zh: 滕州段士雄反，驤討平之。

translations.literal: Duan Shixiong of Tengzhou rebelled; Ziang campaigned and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Shixiong of Tengzhou rebelled, Ziang campaigned against him and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 捕倭浙東，斬獲多，擢都督僉事，見親任，嘗掌錦衣衛事，典詔獄。

translations.literal: Pursuing pirates in eastern Zhejiang, he beheaded and captured many; he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Chief Command, was seen as trusted, once managed the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and oversaw imperial prison cases.
translations.idiomatic: In pursuing Japanese pirates in eastern Zhejiang he took many heads and captives; he was promoted to vice commissioner of the chief command, enjoyed the Founder's trust, once managed the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and oversaw the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 後坐胡惟庸黨死。

translations.literal: Later he was executed as a member of Hu Weiyong's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was executed as an associate of Hu Weiyong's faction.

sentences.zh: 楊元杲

translations.literal: Yang Yuangao
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuangao

sentences.zh: 〈（阮弘道）〉

translations.literal: (Ruan Hongdao)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ruan Hongdao)]〉

sentences.zh: 楊元杲、阮弘道，皆滁人，家世皆儒者。

translations.literal: Yang Yuangao and Ruan Hongdao were both men of Chuzhou; their families for generations were Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuangao and Ruan Hongdao were both natives of Chuzhou, from families of Confucian scholars for generations.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，同為行省左右司員外郎，與陶安等更番掌行機宜文字。

translations.literal: Following the river crossing, they both served as vice directors of the left and right sections of the branch secretariat, and with Tao An and others took turns managing urgent administrative documents.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangzi they both served as vice directors of the left and right sections of the branch secretariat, and with Tao An and others took turns handling urgent administrative documents.

sentences.zh: 元杲以郎中擢理軍儲於金華，而弘道亦於是歲以郎中從大都督文正守南昌，皆有功。

translations.literal: Yuangao was promoted from director to manage military supplies at Jinhua, while Hongdao in the same year as director followed Grand General Wen Zheng in defending Nanchang—both had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangao was promoted from director to manage military supplies at Jinhua, while Hongdao in the same year, also as director, followed Grand General Wen Zheng in defending Nanchang; both performed with merit.

sentences.zh: 二人皆於太祖最故，又皆儒雅，嗜文學，練達政體，而元杲知慮尤周密。

translations.literal: Both men were among the Founder's oldest associates, and both were refined and literary, devoted to letters, proficient in government—and Yuangao's forethought was especially thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Both were among the Founder's oldest associates; both were refined and literary, devoted to letters, and skilled in the ways of government, though Yuangao's forethought was especially thorough.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「文臣從渡江，掌簿書文字，勤勞十餘年，無如楊元杲、阮弘道、李夢庚、侯元善、樊景昭者。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once said: "Among civil officials who crossed the river and managed ledgers and documents, laboring over ten years, none compare to Yang Yuangao, Ruan Hongdao, Li Menggeng, Hou Yuanshan, and Fan Jingzhao."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once said, "Among the civil officials who crossed the Yangzi and managed ledgers and documents, laboring for more than ten years, none compare with Yang Yuangao, Ruan Hongdao, Li Menggeng, Hou Yuanshan, and Fan Jingzhao."

sentences.zh: 其後，元杲歷應天府尹，弘道歷福建、江西行省參政，皆卒官。

translations.literal: Afterward Yuangao served as prefect of Yingtian, and Hongdao served as branch secretariat commissioner in Fujian and Jiangxi—both died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Yuangao served as prefect of Yingtian, and Hongdao served as branch secretariat commissioner in Fujian and Jiangxi; both died in office.

sentences.zh: 元杲子賁，博學強記，以詞翰知名，薦授大名知縣，仕至周府紀善。

translations.literal: Yuangao's son Ben was learned with a strong memory, renowned for literary composition; recommended, he was appointed magistrate of Daming, and served up to secretary of the Zhou princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangao's son Ben was broadly learned with a powerful memory and was renowned for his writing; on recommendation he was appointed magistrate of Daming and rose to secretary of the Zhou princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 元善，全椒人，歷官參知政事，與樊景昭俱無所表見。

translations.literal: Yuanshan was a man of Quanjiao; he served as vice grand councillor; he and Fan Jingzhao alike left nothing noteworthy on record.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yuanshan, a native of Quanjiao, served as vice grand councillor; he and Fan Jingzhao alike left nothing noteworthy on record.

sentences.zh: 附 汪河

translations.literal: Appended: Wang He
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Wang He

sentences.zh: 又汪河者，舒城人。

translations.literal: There was also Wang He, a man of Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wang He, a native of Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 嘗師余闕，以文章名。

translations.literal: He once studied under Yu Que and was famed for his literary writing.
translations.idiomatic: He had once studied under Yu Que and was famed for his literary writing.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，為行中書省掾，數陳時務。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the river and served as clerk of the Branch Secretariat, repeatedly presenting affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Founder's crossing of the Yangzi and served as a clerk of the branch secretariat, repeatedly presenting policy advice.

sentences.zh: 太祖高其才，進大都督府都事。

translations.literal: The Founder valued his talent and advanced him to Chief Clerk of the Great Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder valued his talent and promoted him to chief clerk of the great military commission.

sentences.zh: 使察罕，議論稱旨。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Chahan, his discussions won approval.
translations.idiomatic: Sent as envoy to Chahan, his discussions won the Founder's approval.

sentences.zh: 後奉命偕錢楨至河南，報擴廓聘，為所留。

translations.literal: Later ordered together with Qian Zhen to go to Henan to report on Köke Temür's marriage proposal, he was detained by them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, ordered to go with Qian Zhen to Henan to report on Köke Temür's marriage proposal, he was detained.

sentences.zh: 太祖前後七致擴廓書，終不報。

translations.literal: The Founder seven times in succession sent letters to Köke Temür, yet in the end received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent seven letters to Köke Temür in succession, yet received no reply.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，大軍下河、洛，擴廓走定西，河始得歸，被拘凡六年。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year 1 the great army descended on the He and Luo regions; Köke Temür fled to Dingxi; He was only then able to return, having been detained altogether six years.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 the main army descended on the He and Luo regions; Köke Temür fled to Dingxi; He was only then able to return, having been held for six years.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉之，進吏部侍郎，備陳西征方略。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly commended him and advanced him to Vice Minister of Personnel, presenting in full the strategy for the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor greatly commended him and promoted him to vice minister of personnel, presenting in detail the strategy for the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 二年改御史臺侍御史。

translations.literal: In year 2 he was changed to Attendant Censor of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was made an attendant censor of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜晉王左相，親御便殿諭遣之。

translations.literal: In year 9 he was appointed Left Counselor of the Prince of Jin; the Emperor personally received him in the side hall to instruct and send him off.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was appointed left counselor to the Prince of Jin; the Emperor personally received him in the side hall to instruct and send him off.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，卒於官。

translations.literal: After several years in office, he died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office, he died in his post.

sentences.zh: 孔克仁

translations.literal: Kong Keren
translations.idiomatic: Kong Keren

sentences.zh: 孔克仁，句容人。

translations.literal: Kong Keren was a man of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Keren was a native of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 由行省都事進郎中。

translations.literal: He advanced from chief clerk of the branch secretariat to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from chief clerk of the branch secretariat to director.

sentences.zh: 嘗偕宋濂侍太祖，太祖數與論天下形勢及前代興亡事。

translations.literal: He once accompanied Song Lian in attending the Founder; the Founder repeatedly discussed with them the world's strategic situation and the rise and fall of former dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: He once attended the Founder together with Song Lian, and the Founder often discussed with them the strategic situation of the realm and the rise and fall of earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒既滅，太祖志圖中原，謂克仁曰：「元運既隳，豪傑互爭，其釁可乘。

translations.literal: After Chen Youliang was destroyed, the Founder set his sights on the Central Plains and said to Keren: "The Yuan mandate is already broken; heroes contend with one another—the opening can be seized.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Youliang was destroyed, the Founder turned his ambitions toward the Central Plains and said to Kong, "The Yuan mandate is already broken and rival lords contend with one another; the opening can be seized.

sentences.zh: 吾欲督兩淮、江南諸郡之民，及時耕種，加以訓練。

translations.literal: I wish to oversee the people of the Two Huai and Jiangnan commanderies, sow and plow in season, and also train them.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to oversee the people of the Two Huai and the Jiangnan commanderies, have them sow and plow in season, and train them as well.

sentences.zh: 兵農兼資，進取退守。

translations.literal: With both military and agricultural resources, we can advance or retreat and hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: With both military and agricultural resources in hand, we can advance or hold our ground.

sentences.zh: 仍於兩淮間饋運可通之處，儲糧以俟。

translations.literal: Moreover at places in the Two Huai where supply transport can pass, store grain and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at points between the Two Huai where supply lines can pass, we should store grain and wait.

sentences.zh: 兵食既足，中原可圖。

translations.literal: When troops and provisions are sufficient, the Central Plains can be targeted.
translations.idiomatic: Once troops and provisions are sufficient, the Central Plains can be taken.

sentences.zh: 卿以為何如？」

translations.literal: What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you think of this?"

sentences.zh: 克仁對曰：「積糧訓兵，觀釁待時，此長策也。」

translations.literal: Keren replied: "Accumulating grain and training troops, watching for openings and awaiting the time—this is the long-term strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Kong replied, "To accumulate grain and train troops, watch for openings and await the right moment—this is the long-term strategy."

sentences.zh: 當是時，江左兵勢日盛，太祖以漢高自期，嘗謂克仁曰：「秦政暴虐，漢高帝起布衣，以寬大馭群雄，遂為天下主。

translations.literal: At that time military strength east of the river grew daily; the Founder measured himself against Emperor Gaozu of Han and once said to Keren: "Qin rule was cruel and tyrannical; Emperor Gaozu rose from common cloth, used magnanimity to control the rival lords, and thus became ruler of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time military strength east of the Yangzi grew daily; the Founder measured himself against Emperor Gaozu of Han and once said to Kong, "Qin rule was cruel and tyrannical; Emperor Gaozu rose from common cloth, governed the rival lords with magnanimity, and thus became ruler of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今群雄蜂起，皆不知修法度以明軍政，此其所以無成也。」

translations.literal: Now rival lords swarm forth, all failing to establish regulations and clarify military government—this is why they cannot succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Now rival lords swarm forth, yet none know how to establish regulations and clarify military government—this is why they cannot succeed."

sentences.zh: 因感嘆久之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed at length.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「天下用兵，河北有孛羅帖木兒，河南有擴廓帖木兒，關中有李思齊、張良弼。

translations.literal: He also said: "Under arms across the realm, in Hebei there is Boluo Temür, in Henan there is Köke Temür, and in Guanzhong there are Li Siqi and Zhang Liangbi.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Across the realm at war, Hebei has Boluo Temür, Henan has Köke Temür, and Guanzhong has Li Siqi and Zhang Liangbi.

sentences.zh: 然有兵而無紀律者河北也；

translations.literal: Yet Hebei has troops but no discipline;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hebei has troops but no discipline;

sentences.zh: 稍有紀律而兵不振者河南也；

translations.literal: Henan has some discipline but its troops are not vigorous;
translations.idiomatic: Henan has some discipline but its armies lack vigor;

sentences.zh: 道途不通、饋餉不繼者關中也。

translations.literal: Guanzhong has roads blocked and supply lines cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong has blocked roads and broken supply lines.

sentences.zh: 江南則惟我與張士誠耳。

translations.literal: In Jiangnan it is only I and Zhang Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan there are only Zhang Shicheng and myself.

sentences.zh: 士誠多奸謀，尚間諜，御眾無紀律。

translations.literal: Shicheng uses many treacherous schemes, favors spies, and commands his troops without discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng relies on treacherous schemes, favors spies, and commands his troops without discipline.

sentences.zh: 我以數十萬眾，修軍政，任將帥，相時而動，其勢有不足平者。」

translations.literal: I with several hundred thousand men, rectifying military government, appointing generals, moving according to the times—their power surely cannot be enough to stand against us."
translations.idiomatic: With several hundred thousand men under me, if we rectify military government, appoint generals, and move according to the times, their strength can surely not be enough to resist us."

sentences.zh: 克仁頓首曰：「主上神武，當定天下於一矣。」

translations.literal: Keren bowed and said: "My lord is divinely martial; you will surely unify the realm as one."
translations.idiomatic: Kong bowed and said, "My lord is divinely martial; you will surely unify the realm."

sentences.zh: 嘗閱《漢書》，濂與克仁侍。

translations.literal: Once when reading the Book of Han, Song and Keren attended.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while reading the Book of Han, Song Lian and Kong Keren were in attendance.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「漢治道不純者何？」

translations.literal: The Founder said: "Why was Han governance not pure?"
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said, "Why was Han governance not pure?"

sentences.zh: 克仁對曰：「王霸雜故也。」

translations.literal: Keren replied: "Because kingship and hegemony were mixed."
translations.idiomatic: Kong replied, "Because kingship and hegemony were mixed."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「誰執其咎？」
