translations.literal: The Founder said: "Who bears the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said, "Who bears the blame?"

sentences.zh: 克仁曰：「責在高祖。」

translations.literal: Keren said: "The fault lies with Gaozu."
translations.idiomatic: Kong said, "The fault lies with Gaozu."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「高祖創業，遭秦滅學，民憔悴甫蘇，禮樂之事固所未講。

translations.literal: The Founder said: "Gaozu founded the enterprise, met with Qin's destruction of learning, the people worn and just recovering—matters of ritual and music were naturally not yet discussed.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said, "Gaozu founded the enterprise at a time when Qin had destroyed learning, the people were worn out and only just reviving, and matters of ritual and music had naturally not yet been addressed.

sentences.zh: 孝文為令主，正當制禮作樂，以復三代之舊。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was an excellent ruler; precisely then he should have made rites and music to restore the old of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was an excellent ruler; precisely then he should have made rites and music to restore the institutions of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 乃逡巡未遑，使漢業終於如是。

translations.literal: Yet he hesitated and had no leisure, so Han's enterprise ended thus.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he hesitated and had no leisure for it, and so Han's enterprise ended as it did.

sentences.zh: 帝王之道，貴不違時。

translations.literal: The way of emperors and kings values not violating the right time.
translations.idiomatic: The way of emperors and kings lies in not acting against the proper time.

sentences.zh: 三代之王有其時而能為之，漢文有其時而不為，周世宗則無其時而為之者也。」

translations.literal: Kings of the Three Dynasties had their time and could act; Han Wen had his time but did not act; Emperor Shizong of Zhou had no time yet acted."
translations.idiomatic: The kings of the Three Dynasties had their time and were able to act; Emperor Wen of Han had his time but did not act; Emperor Shizong of Zhou had no proper time yet acted anyway."

sentences.zh: 又嘗問克仁：「漢高起徒步為萬乘主，所操何道？」

translations.literal: He also once asked Keren: "Gaozu of Han rose from footsoldier to lord of ten thousand chariots—what Way did he practice?"
translations.idiomatic: He also once asked Kong, "Gaozu of Han rose from a foot soldier to lord of ten thousand chariots—what Way did he follow?"

sentences.zh: 克仁對曰：「知人善任使。」

translations.literal: Keren replied: "Knowing men and appointing them well."
translations.idiomatic: Kong replied, "Knowing men and employing them well."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「項羽南面稱孤，仁義不施，而自矜功伐。

translations.literal: The Founder said: "Xiang Yu faced south and called himself a lone ruler, showed no benevolence and righteousness, yet prided himself on merit and bragged of his victories.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said, "Xiang Yu faced south and styled himself a lone ruler, showed no benevolence or righteousness, yet prided himself on merit and boasted of his victories.

sentences.zh: 高祖知其然，承以柔遜，濟以寬仁，卒以勝之。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew this; he met it with soft humility and aided it with generous benevolence, and in the end overcame him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu knew this; he met him with soft humility and aided his cause with generous benevolence, and in the end overcame him.

sentences.zh: 今豪傑非一，我守江左，任賢撫民，以觀天下之變。

translations.literal: Now rival lords are not one; I hold the left bank of the river, appoint the worthy and comfort the people, to watch the changes in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Now rival lords are many; I hold the left bank of the Yangzi, appoint the worthy and comfort the people, and watch the changes in the realm.

sentences.zh: 若徒與角力，則猝難定也。」

translations.literal: If we merely contend in force, sudden settlement will be hard."
translations.idiomatic: If we merely contend in brute force, sudden settlement will be difficult."

sentences.zh: 及徐達等下淮東、西，又謂克仁曰：「壬辰之亂，生民塗炭。

translations.literal: When Xu Da and others took east and west Huai, he again said to Keren: "In the disorder of renchen, the people were burned in fire and crushed on the anvil.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da and others took eastern and western Huai, he again said to Kong, "In the disorder of the renchen year, the people were burned in fire and crushed on the anvil.

sentences.zh: 中原諸將，孛羅擁兵犯闕，亂倫干紀，行已夷滅。

translations.literal: Generals of the Central Plains—Boluo seized troops and violated the palace, violated ethics and rebelled against order; his conduct has already been extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Among the generals of the Central Plains, Boluo seized troops and violated the palace, transgressing ethics and order; his line has already been extinguished.

sentences.zh: 擴廓挾太子以稱戈，急私仇，無敵愾之志。

translations.literal: Köke held the crown prince hostage and raised arms, was urgent about private enmity, and had no will to resist the foreign foe.
translations.idiomatic: Köke held the crown prince hostage and took up arms, pressing private enmities and lacking any will to resist the common foe.

sentences.zh: 思齊輩碌碌，竊據一方，民受其害。

translations.literal: Siqi and his ilk were mediocre, stole and held one region—the people suffered their harm.
translations.idiomatic: Siqi and his ilk are mediocre men who have seized and hold one region, and the people suffer under them.

sentences.zh: 士誠外假元名，反覆兩端。

translations.literal: Shicheng outwardly borrowed the Yuan name but wavered between two sides.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng outwardly borrowed the Yuan name yet wavered between two sides.

sentences.zh: 明玉珍父子據蜀僭號，喜於自用而無遠謀。

translations.literal: Ming Yuzhen and his son held Shu and usurped a title, delighted in acting on their own judgment without long-range plans.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Yuzhen and his son hold Shu and have usurped a title; they delight in acting on their own judgment and lack long-range plans.

sentences.zh: 觀其所為，皆不能有成。

translations.literal: Observing their conduct, none can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by their conduct, none of them can succeed.

sentences.zh: 予揆天時，審人事，有可定之機。

translations.literal: I measure heaven's timing and examine human affairs; there is an opening for conquest.
translations.idiomatic: I have measured heaven's timing and examined human affairs, and there is an opening for conquest.

sentences.zh: 今師西出襄、樊，東逾淮、泗，首尾相應，擊之必勝。

translations.literal: Now our army west out from Xiang and Fan, east over Huai and Si, head and tail responding—strike and we surely win.
translations.idiomatic: Now our armies advance west from Xiang and Fan and east beyond the Huai and Si, head and tail responding to one another; strike and we are sure to win.

sentences.zh: 大事可成，天下不難定。

translations.literal: The great enterprise can be accomplished; the realm is not hard to settle.
translations.idiomatic: The great enterprise can be accomplished, and the realm will not be hard to settle.

sentences.zh: 既定之後，生息猶難，方勞思慮耳。」

translations.literal: After it is settled, restoration and nurturing will still be difficult—that is what will truly tax our thought."
translations.idiomatic: After it is settled, restoration and nurturing will still be difficult—that is what will truly tax our thought."

sentences.zh: 克仁侍帷幄最久，故獲聞太祖謀略居多。

translations.literal: Keren attended in the command tent longest, and so heard most of the Founder's stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Keren attended in the command tent longer than anyone else, and so heard more of the Founder's stratagems than the others.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年四月，命克仁等授諸子經，功臣子弟亦令入學。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Hongwu, Keren and others were ordered to teach the classics to the princes; sons of meritorious ministers were also ordered to enter school.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Hongwu year 2, Kong and others were ordered to teach the classics to the princes, and the sons of meritorious ministers were also ordered to enter school.

sentences.zh: 已，出知江州，入為參議，坐事死。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as prefect of Jiangzhou, entered as deliberator, and was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went out as prefect of Jiangzhou, then returned as deliberator, and was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：太祖起布衣，經營天下。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Founder rose from common cloth and managed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: The Founder rose from common cloth and set about winning the realm.

sentences.zh: 渡江以來，規模宏遠，聲教風馳。

translations.literal: Since crossing the river, his scope was vast and far-reaching, and his civilizing influence spread like wind.
translations.idiomatic: Since crossing the Yangzi, his designs have been vast and far-reaching, and his civilizing influence has spread like the wind.

sentences.zh: 雖曰天授，抑亦左右丞弼多國士之助歟。

translations.literal: Although one may say it was heaven's gift, was it not also that left and right ministers and assistants had many nation-gifted scholars to help?
translations.idiomatic: Although one may call it heaven's gift, was it not also because the ministers and assistants at his side included many men of national talent?

sentences.zh: 陳遇見禮不下劉基，而超然利祿之外。

translations.literal: Chen Yu received honor no less than Liu Ji, yet stood aloof beyond salary and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu received honor no less than Liu Ji, yet stood aloof from salary and rank.

sentences.zh: 葉兌於天下大計，籌之審矣，亦能抗節肥遯，其高致均非人所易及。

translations.literal: Ye Dui on the great designs for the realm deliberated with thoroughness, and could also uphold integrity and withdraw into reclusion—his lofty character alike is not what ordinary men can easily reach.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Dui deliberated with thoroughness on the great designs for the realm, and could also uphold his integrity and withdraw into reclusion; his lofty character, too, is not easily matched.

sentences.zh: 孔克仁無可稱述，以太祖之雄謀大略具其事中，故敘列於篇。

translations.literal: Kong Keren has nothing specially worth recounting; because the Founder's heroic stratagems and great designs are fully contained in the affairs involving him, he is therefore listed in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Keren has nothing especially worth recounting in his own right; because the Founder's heroic stratagems and great designs are fully preserved in the affairs in which he appears, he is therefore included in this chapter.
